objective: Falsify whether the review mechanism can reconstruct authoritative truth from contradictory raw evidence without proposer conclusions.
hypothesis: A deterministic hierarchy can identify admissible authority and expose unresolved contradictions; the reviewer can then reconstruct the winning current claim without relying on a proposer summary.
rules: Explicit supersession beats older evidence within the same authority lineage.
Current authoritative implementation/design/QA outrank historical discussion and model reasoning.
A contradiction between same-rank current authoritative objects must remain unresolved and non-promotable unless a deterministic supersession relation resolves it.
Proposer conclusions are not inputs to the reconstruction function.
Missing provenance or malformed source class fails closed.
failure_conditions: historical or non-authoritative evidence defeats current authoritative evidence
same-rank unresolved contradiction is silently collapsed
superseded evidence is treated as current
proposer conclusion is required to choose a winner
